articles.title: Ilia Topuria Hasn't Said a Word...
articles.description: Ilia Topuria has not said a word, and Chael Sonnen says that silence might be the smartest marketing move in MMA right now. Chael starts with Brock Lesnar, the one monster Vince McMahon would not let speak, because monsters do not talk. Paul Heyman did the talking for him. From there, Chael explains why marketing is never a guarantee, it is an experiment, and sometimes the accident wins. Nick Diaz no-showing the Georges St-Pierre press conference left an empty chair that Dana White thought had ruined the event. It became one of the most successful press conferences of all time. Topuria is running the same play right now, whether he knows it or not. He might be the hottest name at 155 pounds, maybe in all of MMA, and he can pick his opponent and his date. Paddy Pimblett is chasing him and playing it perfectly, but Chael explains why Topuria gains nothing by answering. The fight is huge either way. Then Chael asks the question nobody in the community has suggested out loud: what if Topuria is thinking about retiring? The money, the two-division world titles, the short career, it is all there. And saying it out loud might be exactly the prod that gets him talking. Watch to the end, then tell us in the comments: is the silence strategy, or is it an accident? Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Being quiet is seldom helpful in this business 0:43 Marketing is an experiment, nobody can guarantee it 1:22 Nick Diaz, the empty chair, and the accident that sold a fight 1:58 Topuria has said nothing, and it is working 2:34 The hottest name at 155 can pick his opponent and date 3:28 Paddy is chasing Topuria, and Topuria does not need to answer 4:28 The retirement question nobody is asking 5:17 Chael is inviting Topuria on to speak 5:51 Staying quiet makes us want to hear from him even more #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria

articles.title: Paddy Called Dana vs Eddie the Dumbest Thing Ever
articles.description: The Dana White versus Eddie Hearn feud rolls on, and Chael Sonnen closes it out with the two questions nobody else is asking: what is Fury versus Joshua actually worth, and what does Eddie get if he wins? Chael's first answer will annoy people. Fury versus AJ is not as big as they are pretending it is. It will do a very good night of business if it is the only show in town, but for years Chael has said these two are fighting for nothing: no title, no contendership, no ranking, two men in seemingly their final fight out for one last cash grab. Now he has been corrected, because they have produced a world title, and Chael tells the full Mayweather versus Conor McGregor money belt story to show what a produced title is worth, including the lost billion-dollar belt he personally had to guard until security came for it. His question is simple: did Oleksandr Usyk hand them one of his belts? Then the feud itself. If Eddie wins, he does not leave a bigger promoter than Dana in power, connections, networks, distribution, or events, so Paddy Pimblett has a point that it is silly. But Eddie has already threatened to pull AJ, and Dana has not played his card. The man who owns the building that night can have Eddie removed, and Chael wants Paddy asked again whether it is still ridiculous, or actually pretty fun. Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Paddy called Dana vs Eddie the dumbest thing ever 0:28 Producer trumps promoter: Dana is both 0:56 The promoter's license question: whose name goes on it? 1:25 The ring is the stage 1:53 Eddie's nuclear option: pull AJ 3:01 Somebody is in charge of that building 3:50 Fury vs AJ is not as big as they are pretending 4:17 They produced a world title: the Mayweather vs Conor money belt 5:40 Did Usyk give them a belt to fight for? 6:17 If Eddie wins the feud, what does he get? 7:29 Dana owns the building and could have Eddie removed #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #EddieHearn

articles.title: Bruce Buffer Finds Josh Hokit Disrespectful
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael #HumeHealth #smartscale #weightloss Bruce Buffer told BJPenn.com he finds Josh Hokit disrespectful, and Chael Sonnen finds that fascinating, starting with who said it. Bruce is one of the highest paid people in the UFC and he never throws a punch. If anyone alive understands the power of words, it is the man who built a fortune using only words. Chael's first problem with the comment: Josh Hokit is trying to be disrespectful. That is the act, and it is working. If Bruce had found him respectful, Josh would have failed. Chael puts him in a line with Elvis Presley, whose hip shaking scandalized a generation of parents without a single profane word, and with Chael himself, whose G-rated routine never used profanity and still got him labeled the greatest trash talker in sports, and got a union-funded legal fight to keep him from being licensed. Then the results argument. Hokit fought on the White House lawn and is about to fight at Madison Square Garden for the undisputed championship, the fastest path to a title shot since Brock Lesnar, with sponsors remodeling his house for the cameras coming. Take every word he ever said away and ask if he is in the same spot. He is not. So if this is disrespect, Chael's verdict is that disrespect is a wonderful part of the sport, and in ten years Hokit will not be remembered as disrespectful. He will be copied, and remembered as innovative. articles.title: Does Sean Strickland Want to Fight?
articles.description: The Strickland story gets stranger, and Chael Sonnen is now ruling out his own best theories one by one. Somebody new always seems to show up in a fighter's life, somebody with a tie to Hollywood who promises to make them famous and tells them how underpaid they are. Chael's problem with that theory: not one single athlete, not one single time, ever got what that person promised. He tests the money theory against Tim Sylvia. Sylvia never thought he was underpaid until Brock Lesnar was brought in, made champion, and paid 20 times what Sylvia was getting, and that is what got him sideways with the UFC. Could a rumor about somebody else's money have done the same to Sean Strickland? Chael doubts it. Sean is one of the best paid guys in the sport, and neither his last opponent nor his next one makes more than he does. So what changed? Chael admits he does not know, but he senses Sean is not going to get his way, and he points to Dana White's own words: the UFC is dealing with this with Sean right now, and it has dealt with it consistently, with somebody, the whole time Dana has been there. Chael also explains why he does not need a Strickland vs Imavov rematch, why Imavov should get the title shot, and why Sean himself agrees. Then Chael tells the story of his own day of realization, on a hill at 6:45 on a Sunday morning at 36 years old, when everything changed and nobody had gotten to him at all. Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Dana on Strickland: sideways with two of 700 athletes 1:04 What changed with Sean? 1:48 Pricing yourself out is how you say you don't want to fight 2:40 Cejudo gave the belt back and lost the PPV points 3:57 Somebody got a hold of Tom Aspinall 5:47 Tim Sylvia got sideways over Brock Lesnar's pay 7:10 Dana: we've dealt with this consistently, with somebody 7:39 Imavov deserves the title shot, and Sean agrees 8:12 Chael's day of realization: 6:45 AM, age 36 #ChaelSonnen #UFC #SeanStrickland #DanaWhite #MMA

The Truth About Khamzat Chimaev’s 42-Pound Weight Cut #ufc
articles.description: Did Khamzat Chimaev really lose 42 pounds in a week to fight Sean Strickland? Chael Sonnen says the story is completely false. Chael challenges the reports about Khamzat’s supposed walking weight, arguing that he doesn't believe Chimaev has ever been as heavy as 220 pounds. He points to what he has observed instead: Khamzat appearing relatively small on weigh-in day, even when competing against welterweights. But the bigger question is whether Chimaev should move up to 205 pounds. Chael believes Khamzat could compete at light heavyweight, but says the decision needs to be carefully considered. If Khamzat moves up and becomes champion, Chael doesn't want to see him bouncing back and forth between divisions. Choosing 205 pounds means committing to the division, win or lose. So is Khamzat Chimaev really preparing to move up, or has the conversation about his size gotten ahead of the facts? #ChaelSonnen #KhamzatChimaev #SeanStrickland #UFC #MMA #LightHeavyweight #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Fury Should Show Whether AJ Fights or Not
articles.description: Anthony Joshua is hinting he might not even show up, and Chael Sonnen says Tyson Fury's camp should not flinch for one second. Hold the event. Walk Fury out, raise his hand, and give him the victory, because a win is a win, and the rulebook backs it up. Chael breaks down why a no-show is not a crisis but an ending boxing already wrote for itself. Just like MMA, where disqualification sits on the very same page as the knockout, the TKO, and the submission (ask Aljamain Sterling, who won a world title by DQ), frustrating an opponent into failing is a legitimate path to victory. Fury and Joshua should have fought as amateurs, for Olympic and world teams, and for world championships, yet they have avoided each other for years, and boxing failed to ever bring this match together. Now AJ is taking a victory lap for bringing the fight to England while telling fans to buy tickets and wait to hear if he shows. If Chael were promoting this event, he would be printing the shirts and popping the popcorn, with or without AJ. And with Eddie Hearn and Dana White circling the promotion, the will-he-show drama may be the only hook this fight has left. Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in combat sports, every day. 0:00 Fury is fighting to keep the fight together 1:39 Hold the event whether both sides show or not 4:32 The guy who shows up wins 7:10 Disqualification sits on the same page as KO and TKO 8:17 Boxing failed to bring this match together 9:01 AJ's England victory lap vs. his no-show threat 9:21 If Chael were the promoter, he would not flinch #ChaelSonnen #Boxing #TysonFury #AnthonyJoshua #MMA

articles.title: The ONE Fight That Could Bring Jon Jones Back #ufc
articles.description: Is Jon Jones’ biggest regret really missing the White House UFC event — or is there another fight he wishes he had taken? Chael Sonnen believes Alex Pereira could be at the center of Jones’ comments. And while Jones has said he doesn't know if he'll fight again, Chael points to one important detail: Jones has remained in the UFC’s drug-testing pool. That doesn't guarantee a comeback, but it leaves the door open. According to Chael, the missing ingredient isn't necessarily money or opportunity. It's motivation. Jones needs the right opponent — someone capable of getting under his skin and giving him a reason to compete again. And Chael believes there is one fighter with the skills and ability to do exactly that. Could Alex Pereira be the matchup that finally brings Jon Jones back to the Octagon? #ChaelSonnen #JonJones #AlexPereira #UFC #MMA #UFCWhiteHouse #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews

articles.title: Strickland Promised the Worst Fight Ever
articles.description: Sean Strickland just did something no fighter has ever pulled off, and now he is talking about giving his belt back, moving up to 205 pounds, and putting on the most boring fight ever just to ride out his contract. Chael Sonnen says the strangest part is that it would work. Chael has seen the fighter pay argument in every era since Dana White's run began in 2001, starting with Tito Ortiz comparing his pay to boxing champion Roy Jones Jr. It never got over, because fans could never relate to a fighter saying a million dollars is not enough for 25 minutes of work. Strickland is somehow getting support from all sides. At his son's fifth grade football game, fans came up to Chael talking about Strickland, and they were on his side, on a night Brendan Allen was fighting. Chael breaks down the contract itself: there is no clause that cannot be manipulated either way, and a champion who refuses 170, then refuses 185 after holding that belt too, is never getting closer to the expiration date. Fantasy versus reality, neither one is great. His prediction: it never gets tested. Option C was plan A all along. Strickland defends the championship against Nassourdine Imavov. articles.title: Kayla: Anything Ronda Did, I Can Do Better
articles.description: Kayla Harrison is back, she is getting ready for Amanda Nunes, and she just went straight at Ronda Rousey. Chael Sonnen says he does not fully understand why these two were never allies, one champion passing the torch to the next, but he loves the receipt Kayla just delivered. Kayla laid out the full judo resume side by side: Ronda's Olympic bronze, world silver, a World Cup and a Grand Prix medal, against Kayla's every World Cup, every Grand Prix, every Grand Slam, two Masters titles, a world championship, and two Olympic gold medals. Her closing line said it all: she knew she could do MMA because anything Ronda could do, she could do better. Chael then closes the loop: Ronda cannot get back into the UFC, because the UFC is for tomorrow's champions only, and the only way these two ever meet is if Kayla walks free and Jake Paul calls them both. He also asks why the greats, Jon Jones with Gable Steveson included, give the next great a hard time instead of standing with them. Chael's biggest message: Kayla is back. Kayla vs Amanda was meant to kick off the UFC on Paramount, and he predicts it finally goes down in January, worth the wait after both women took time away. articles.title: You're Looking at Alex Pereira All Wrong
articles.description: Alex Pereira is still hot, and Chael Sonnen says he loves this side of him. Pereira came out and said the influencers and pundits, Daniel Cormier among them, got together and pushed Josh Hokit into a championship fight with Ciryl Gane, a rematch Pereira himself was very much pursuing, and he is not hiding how annoyed he is about it. Chael says that is pure competitor, and it reminds him of a fight that never happened in a cage: Khabib Nurmagomedov against Jon Jones, over the pound-for-pound list. Khabib retired in the cage, said he had done everything he set out to do except one thing, he had never been voted pound-for-pound number one, and he asked for it. The anonymous panel actually did it, moving Khabib to number one and dropping Jones down. Jones fired right back: you do not get to go in front of me because you asked for it, and other guys beat Justin Gaethje too without jumping the line. Chael also breaks down why a Gane rematch is a hard sell right away: Pereira is 0-1 at heavyweight, and the rematch would now be for the undisputed title, not the interim. Pereira has a built-in story with Hokit, needs Hokit to win, has covered both sides, and still has Sergei Pavlovich in front of him. If you are annoyed by Pereira complaining, Chael says you are seeing it wrong. Subscribe for Chael's take on the biggest stories in MMA, every day. 0:00 Pereira is still hot, and Chael loves this side of him 0:12 The genesis: influencers pushed Josh Hokit vs Ciryl Gane 0:47 The fight that never happened in a cage: Khabib vs Jon Jones 0:54 Khabib retires and asks for pound-for-pound number one 1:54 The panel did it: Khabib to number one, Jones dropped down 2:09 Jones fired back: you don't jump me because you asked 2:46 The panel switched it back, and it hurt their integrity 2:57 What caring that much told Chael about both men's greatness 3:12 Why a Gane rematch is hard: 0-1 at heavyweight, now undisputed 4:15 Pereira's built-in story with Josh Hokit, both sides covered 4:51 Pavlovich is the big task in front of him 5:06 Fans are annoyed by the complaining, Chael says they're wrong #ChaelSonnen #MMA #UFC #AlexPereira #JonJones

articles.title: Is Sean Strickland Playing a Dangerous Game With the UFC?#ufc
articles.description: Is Sean Strickland serious about leaving the UFC for a massive boxing payday — or is this a high-stakes game of chicken? Chael Sonnen weighs in on Strickland’s negotiations and explains why he wants Sean to handle the situation face-to-face with UFC leadership. Chael makes it clear that he doesn't want anything bad to happen to Strickland if he's simply negotiating and considering his options. But he senses a standoff developing, with both sides potentially waiting for the other to make the next move. The possibility of crossing over to boxing and securing a much bigger payday adds another layer to the situation. But how far is Strickland willing to take it, and what happens if neither side backs down? Chael explains why a direct conversation could be the best way to resolve the tension before negotiations turn into a bigger problem. Is Strickland genuinely prepared to walk away, or will the UFC find a way to keep him? #ChaelSonnen #SeanStrickland #UFC #Boxing #MMA #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #CombatSports

articles.title: Daniel Cormier RESPONDS to Alex Pereira callout on Josh Hokit-Ciryl Gane heavyweight title fight
articles.description: Daniel Cormier IS BACK, this time after Alex Pereira mentioned DC's name in an interview this week, claiming people like Daniel and others with big followings were the people who pushed the Josh Hokit and Ciryl Gane heavyweight title fight and ultimately why he isn't getting his shot right now. DC responds to Alex Pereira's comments, and reiterates he was NEVER TOLD by the UFC to promote that fight and doubles down saying that Hokit-Gane is the fight to make. Cormier also says Pereira's comments about him "not being champion" after beating Gane are untrue and have to be a misunderstanding, because he never said he wouldn't be champion. DC said beating Gane doesn't make Pereira the UFC GOAT, but it would absolutely make him champion since he'd have the belt. Follow me on all social media platforms! articles.title: Alex Pereira Has a BIG Problem #ufc
articles.description: Did Ciryl Gane expose a weakness in Alex Pereira that could become an even bigger problem against Sergei Pavlovich? Chael Sonnen isn't convinced Pereira simply lost because Gane was bigger. After watching the fight, Chael points to something else: Gane's unusually aggressive forward pressure and the way he forced Pereira to fight on the back foot. Chael has seen Pereira train up close and remains impressed by his ability. But this raises a serious question: **Does Pereira struggle when a powerful striker relentlessly comes forward?** Gane didn't just rely on his size, Chael argues. He may have been the better kickboxer that night. And if that's the real explanation, Pereira has a specific problem to address. But if the size difference was the deciding factor, the challenge against Sergei Pavlovich could be even more concerning. Pavlovich brings heavyweight power and a dangerous striking game of his own. So what did Pereira's loss actually reveal — a technical weakness, a size disadvantage, or both? Chael breaks down the matchup and explains why the answer could determine Pereira's future against heavyweight contenders. #ChaelSonnen #AlexPereira #CirylGane #SergeiPavlovich #UFC #MMA #UFCHeavyweight #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Joshua Kept the Fight in the UK. Big Deal!
articles.description: Anthony Joshua is getting praised as a man of the people for keeping the Tyson Fury fight in the UK. Chael Sonnen is not buying it, and he says Tyson Fury, the guy willing to fight anywhere to make it happen, is the one who got this right. Chael's test is simple: if you do the fight for the people, the people should not be the ones paying for the gesture. Everyone can watch this fight from anywhere and get the same result and the same resolution. Holding it in the UK just means UK fans pay far more to be there live. That is not serving the people, that is reaching in their pocket. Chael contrasts it with Kid Rock's small-venue tour: a hard $20 ticket cap, no promoter allowed to charge more, and 30 minutes of karaoke so fans could say they opened for Kid Rock. That is a man of the people, actions and a real loss, not words. Then Chael names the real story. Fury and Joshua are not fighting for anything, there is nothing on the line, and this fight does well only if nothing runs against it. The fight that matters is Eddie Hearn vs Dana White. Eddie said Dana cannot be on the stage. Chael says the ring is the ultimate stage: if Dana is in it on fight night, Dana wins. Now he wants Ariel Helwani to set the terms with him and accept them publicly. Who wins, Eddie Hearn or Dana White? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. 0:00 Keeping the Fury fight in the UK: big deal? 0:36 Man of the people?
